questions.question: Rate limiting helps security posture by:
options: Allowing unlimited credential stuffing for realism.
Blunting DoS and abusive request patterns against APIs.
Removing passwords so attackers have nothing to steal.
Publishing admin tokens in mobile app binaries.
questions.explanation: A rate limiter prevents DoS attacks, either intentional or unintentional

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: A rate limiter prevents DoS attacks, either intentional or unintentional, by blocking the excess calls. • Reduce cost.

questions.question: Security as an architecture characteristic means:
options: It is optional decoration after the UI ships.
It is a first-class capability that can drive structural decisions.
Only marketers need to worry about account takeover.
Encryption is banned because it slows microbenchmarks.

reference.book: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, 2nd Edition by Mark Richards and Neal Ford
reference.excerpt: For example, if ease of deployment and testability are high priorities, the architect would emphasize good modularity and isolation at the architecture level—an example of an architecture characteristic driving a structural decision.

questions.question: True or false: Client-side enforcement alone is insufficient against malicious actors who forge requests.
questions.explanation: client requests can easily be forged by malicious actors

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Generally speaking, client is an unreliable place to enforce rate limiting because client requests can easily be forged by malicious actors.

questions.question: Least privilege for services typically means:
options: Every service uses the root cloud account for convenience.
Each component gets only the permissions it needs to do its job.
Database credentials are hardcoded into public mobile apps.
All environments share one writable production credential.

reference.book: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, 2nd Edition by Mark Richards and Neal Ford
reference.excerpt: Services are accessed remotely from a UI using a remote access protocol, typically REST.

questions.question: When users are throttled, Xu says the system should:
options: Fail silently with HTTP 200 and an empty body always.
Show clear exceptions/signals that requests were throttled.
Corrupt the user database to discourage retries.
Disable TLS so the response is easier to cache.
questions.explanation: Show clear exceptions to users when their requests are throttled

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Show clear exceptions to users when their requests are throttled. • High fault tolerance.
